failure.message: The term 'Invoke-JsonUtf8' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable program.
failure.root_cause: scripts/lib/AgentUpdate.ps1 New-CoreDeviceFetcher returned { Invoke-JsonUtf8 ... }.GetNewClosure(). GetNewClosure binds a script block to a new dynamic module linked to the GLOBAL session state, which cannot see a function dot-sourced into a SCRIPT scope - and install-device-service.ps1 dot-sources every library into its own script scope. Reproduced from a clean powershell.exe -NoProfile process: as `-File script.ps1` the name resolves (the script IS the top-level scope), as `& script.ps1` it raises CommandNotFoundException. Every harness in scripts/tests runs with -File, and the M18.4 unit tests inject a fake fetch script block, so the real fetcher had never been invoked by anything.
failure.second_defect: Test-AgentHeartbeatOnCore retried a CommandNotFoundException for the full 90 s and then reported 'Cloud Core does not see the candidate', and the installer printed 'the fault is in Cloud Core's device row, not in this candidate' about a fault that was its own - it had never sent a request. An empty reading and a reading of emptiness are different evidence.

findings: The row is COMPLETE for the gate's purposes: presence, software_version at the top level AND under health, the capability list and capability_count are all present. The 2026-09-08 'Cloud Core carries no software version at all' contract fault is fixed, and this row proves it against production.

The row currently describes the RESTORED release (0.1.0, 29 capabilities) with a six-second heartbeat, so the rollback overwrote the row exactly as expected - the last question of the independent investigation, answered yes.

The candidate would have announced 0.6.0: PagentOS.Agent.Core/Protocol/ProtocolConstants.cs sets AgentInfo.SoftwareVersion = "0.6.0", and Program.cs sends that value in hello. The restored release predates that constant, which is why the row says 0.1.0.

cloud_core_candidate_registration.verdict: PROVEN_REAL - the candidate DID register with Cloud Core as 0.6.0 with 85 capabilities. Only the installer failed to read it.
cloud_core_candidate_registration.how: app/broker/ws.py handles one handshake: service.start_device_session() writes a durable device_sessions row carrying software_version and the hello's full capability list in connection_metadata_json, and service.apply_hello() overwrites devices.software_version and devices.capabilities_json from the same hello. So a session row is a permanent record of what the devices row held at that moment - and unlike the devices row, a rollback does not erase it.

sessions.note: THE CANDIDATE. It connected 1.0 s after the service started and held the connection for the whole 90.6 s the installer spent failing to ask a question.
the rolled-back release, 1.9 s after the candidate's connection ended
the 2026-09-08 attempt, -DisplayPower only. Its candidate reached Cloud Core too.

cloud_core_candidate_registration.consequence: The health gate compares the candidate's version and its capability names against the row. Cloud Core held 0.6.0 and all 85 names, with no name announced twice (entries == distinct names in the session row). Had the fetcher resolved, the gate would have PASSED and the install would have committed. The only defect between the owner and item 28 was the closure.
